months.2: Winter conditions persist, keeping desert tortoises and chuckwallas in brumation. Coyotes and roadrunners remain active during daylight hours, and Peninsular bighorn sheep are occasionally spotted in Indian Canyons.
months.5: As daytime temperatures rise, desert tortoises and chuckwallas shift their activity to cooler morning hours. Coyotes and black-tailed jackrabbits are frequently seen at dawn and dusk.
months.7: With desert floor temperatures regularly topping 100°F, wildlife viewing is strictly limited to dawn and dusk when coyotes and jackrabbits emerge. Mount San Jacinto's cooler high elevations offer occasional sightings of mule deer.
months.11: As winter approaches, desert reptiles enter brumation and disappear from view. Coyotes and black-tailed jackrabbits are frequently seen active throughout the cooler days, and Peninsular bighorn sheep are occasionally spotted in Indian Canyons.

belfast-giants-causeway.overview: Grey and harbor seals haul out along the Causeway Coast and Strangford Lough. Inland, elusive red squirrels inhabit the western Fermanagh woodlands, while the native Irish hare lives in the uplands, including the Mourne Mountains. Coastal waters occasionally yield harbor porpoise sightings from cliffside vantage points.

months.3: Native Irish hares are active across open pastures and upland moors. Wintering geese begin departing Strangford Lough, while seals haul out along the rocky northern coast.
months.4: Marquee seabirds, including Atlantic puffins, begin arriving at the sea cliffs of Rathlin Island to breed. Irish hares remain active in upland pastures, and seals are seen along the Causeway Coast.
months.6: Atlantic puffins and thousands of other breeding seabirds crowd the Rathlin Island cliffs. Summer's calmer seas make it easier to watch the Causeway Coast for harbor porpoises.
